name: Salyut 1
dispatch: Salyut 1 was the first space station in history — launched in April 1971, two years ahead of America's Skylab, and the moment the Soviet Union turned its lead in endurance into a permanent presence in orbit. Its triumph was also its tragedy: the first crew to live aboard it, Soyuz 11, died during their return when a valve vented their cabin to vacuum, and the station was never occupied again. It proved a station could be built and reached — and, at the highest cost, taught the lesson that reshaped every crewed spacecraft after it.
description: The world’s first space station — launched 1971, occupied for 23 days by the Soyuz 11 crew (Dobrovolski, Volkov, Patsayev), all of whom died on return when their capsule depressurised. Salyut 1 was deorbited later that year.
